newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND SEEKS 1.8 PCT GDP BUDGET GAP IN '98 -C.BANK.
newsitem.headline: POLAND SEEKS 1.8 PCT GDP BUDGET GAP IN '98 -C.BANK.

text.p: The Polish Finance Ministry is working on a national budget for 1998 which envisions deficit of 1.8 percent of GDP against the planned 2.8 percent budget gap in 1998, the central bank president said on Tuesday.
"Because of the current account gap and difficulties in financing this year's budget, the (budget) deficit will have to be much lower (next year)," Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz told reporters.
"I know that Finance Minister Marek Belka is preparing it (next year's budget deficit) at about 1.8 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP)," she said.
She said that such a low budget decifit would allow the central bank to loosen its restrictive monetary policy.
